title: nsmbtool placeable object catalog
description: Every custom object that can be dropped into a level, one entry per `stage:` variant. Written by `nsmbtool glue` from NCPatcher's module dump. This is the palette a level editor offers, and the mapping from what it shows to what it must write.

stageObjectIdBase.description: Where the vanilla stage object table ends -- 325. An editor allocates stage object ids upward from here, one per distinct hash it places in a level, starting at this number and contiguous. Reported rather than assumed so that a consumer does not hardcode it a second time.

stageObjects.description: Sorted by module, component, object and variant. An object declaring no `stage:` variants is not placeable and does not appear.

name.description: `module.Object.Variant` -- `coop.CoopFlagActor.Default`. The durable name of this placeable entry.

hash.description: FNV-1a/32 of `name`. THIS IS WHAT A LEVEL STORES, and the only thing here that is stable across builds. Neither id below is: they are compile-time or per-level numbers that have to agree with themselves and nothing more. So a published hash must never change, and `module.Object.Variant` is a compatibility surface -- renaming any of the three parts orphans every level that placed it.

component.description: The component that declares the object. A level may place an entry whose component the ROM was built without; the runtime finds no matching hash and the object does not appear.

variant.description: Which `stage:` variant of that class this is. One class with `stage: [Default, Big]` is two entries here and one entry in the object table.

objectId.description: The OBJECT id: which class the game spawns, allocated upward from 0x182 at build time, ONE PER OBJECT. Every variant of one class shares it -- two entries with the same objectId is correct, not a duplicate. Do not confuse this with the stage object id, which is a different number in a different table: see below.

info.description: The `ObjectInfo` this variant supplies, as a qualified C++ name -- `CoopFlagActor::ObjectInfo_Default`. It holds the placement geometry the game needs at load time, before the actor exists, which is why it is a table rather than something the class could answer for itself.

header.description: The header declaring the class, relative to a module include directory.
